subject: Climate & Environment
title: Wildfire Smoke and Air Quality
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Wildfire Smoke and Air Quality.

hook.text: In 2023, Canadian wildfire smoke turned New York City's sky orange and its air toxic.

buildup.text: Wildfire smoke contains fine particles, carbon monoxide, and toxic chemicals from burned material.

discovery.text: PM2.5 particles from smoke penetrate deep into lungs and enter the bloodstream.

twist.text: Smoke can travel thousands of kilometers. Fires in Siberia degrade air quality in Alaska.

climax.text: Wildfire smoke now affects more people than the fires themselves — a growing global health crisis.

punchline.text: You don't need to live near a fire to breathe one.

quiz.question: How far can wildfire smoke travel?

details.summary: Wildfire smoke contains PM2.5, CO, ozone precursors, and toxic compounds that can travel thousands of kilometers, degrading air quality for hundreds of millions of people far from the fire. Smoke exposure causes respiratory and cardiovascular harm comparable to industrial pollution.
details.whyItMatters: Wildfire smoke is becoming a major public health crisis. As fire seasons lengthen, smoke exposure affects people who will never see a flame.
takeaways: Wildfire smoke can travel across continents and oceans
PM2.5 from fires causes respiratory and cardiovascular harm
Canadian wildfires in 2023 blanketed the US East Coast in hazardous smoke

faq.question: How far can wildfire smoke travel?
faq.answer: Smoke from large fires can be lofted into the upper atmosphere and travel thousands of kilometers. Australian bushfire smoke in 2020 circled the globe, and Canadian fires in 2023 turned skies orange in New York City.

faq.question: Is wildfire smoke more dangerous than urban air pollution?
faq.answer: Studies suggest wildfire PM2.5 may be more toxic per unit mass than urban pollution because it contains more oxidative compounds. However, exposure is typically episodic rather than chronic, and both types cause significant health harm.
